page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8y.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized server instance powered by the custom Alibaba Yitian YiTian710 processor operating at 2.75 GHz. Built on KVM virtualization, it provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, giving a total of 8 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 16 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Cache resources comprise 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 64 MB L3 cache array. Network connectivity offers a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. This instance configuration omits bundled local storage and discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the average middle tier across general processing metrics. Multi-core stress-ng testing returned a score of 14489.92, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 6803.65. Large uncached memory reads reached 96.36 GB/sec, while large uncached memory writes recorded 41.19 GB/sec. Application testing showed average performance with static web serving throughput of 12.71 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 13.18 million operations per second. Hardware cryptographic capabilities include dedicated AES acceleration, though PassMark encryption tests scored low at 1320.86. Small 135M model LLM text generation delivered 186.85 tokens/sec, but performance degraded on 7B models down to 8.46 tokens/sec.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU proportion highlights a compute-dense profile intended for processing workloads rather than memory-heavy datasets. Because local storage is absent, persistent storage relies on external network volumes. The combination of dedicated ARM cores and balanced memory bandwidth provides efficient compute resource utilization for web hosting, API microservices, CI/CD code compilation, and lightweight ETL pipelines, while intensive cryptographic operations, large model LLM processing, and GPU workloads represent key tradeoffs.

It features 8 vCPUs, 16 GB of memory, 64 MB of L3 cache, and a 5 Gbps baseline network throughput without bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals solid middle-tier performance, including a multi-core stress-ng score of 14489.92, static web serving output of 12.71 GB/sec, and 13.18 million Redis SET operations per second. However, encryption benchmarks and 7B model LLM generation reflect lower performance tiers. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers efficient resource density suitable for web microservices, application servers, and light data processing.
